title: Finite generation of the canonical reduction of a strict affinoid
statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. A Tate algebra $T_r=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_rangle$ is the restricted-series ring of [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with Gauss norm $\|\sum a_
u X^
u\|_G=\sup_
u|a_
u|$. Let $C
e0$ be a reduced quotient of such an algebra with its affinoid Banach topology. Define $ho(c)=\sup_\chi|\chi(c)|$, where $\chi:C	o K$ runs over continuous unital $K$-algebra homomorphisms. Put $V=\{a\in K:|a|\le1\}$, $\mathfrak m=\{a\in K:|a|<1\}$, $\kappa=V/\mathfrak m$, $C_{\le1}=\{c:ho(c)\le1\}$ and $C_{<1}=\{c:ho(c)<1\}$. Then $\widetilde C=C_{\le1}/C_{<1}$ is a finitely generated $\kappa$-algebra: there are $t\ge0$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_t\in C_{\le1}$ such that their classes generate $\widetilde C$ as a $\kappa$-algebra. Here generation means that every class is a polynomial in these classes with coefficients in $\kappa$.

source.place: BGR sections 6.3–6.4, finiteness of the reduction algebra. Confirmed in Fargues, Groupes analytiques rigides p-divisibles, section 1.7.1, printed p.18, paragraph defining A-tilde; read online 2026-10-24. That paper works p-adically; the present arbitrary-characteristic statement is the BGR strict-affinoid input, not an extension of the p-adic theorem by assertion. Archival copy WANTED; not present in this checkout.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-affinoid-spectral-banach-norm], $\rho$ is a nonarchimedean submultiplicative $K$-algebra norm. Thus $C_{\le1}$ is a subring and $C_{<1}$ an ideal in it; constants induce the stated $\kappa$-algebra structure. Apply [lem-trf-tate-normalization-lift] to a presentation $C=T_r/I$; $I$ is proper since $C\ne0$. Obtain $A=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$ and a finite injective $K$-algebra map $\varphi:A\to C$. The source is reduced: it embeds as the restricted-series subring of the formal power series domain over $K$ (the first nonzero homogeneous terms of a product have nonzero product). This also covers $d=0$, when $A=K$.

source.place: BGR Theorem 6.3.5/1, finite map implies finite reduction map. Independently read in Temkin, A new proof of the Gerritzen-Grauert theorem, introduction printed p.2 and section 2 (definition of reduction); https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Gerritzen_Grauert.pdf. BGR archival copy WANTED; source is not locally present.

proof.text: Identify $\widetilde A$ with $\kappa[U_1,\ldots,U_d]$. Indeed [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus] gives $\rho_A=\|\cdot\|_G$. Its maximal-ideal formula equals the continuous-character formula here: the same node makes every maximal residue field finite over the algebraically closed $K$, hence equal to $K$; its quotient-Gauss bound makes each resulting evaluation continuous. Conversely a $K$-character has maximal kernel. Reduction of coefficients of a series of Gauss norm at most one gives a polynomial, since only finitely many coefficients have absolute value one. The coefficients that have absolute value below one have supremum strictly below one: outside a finite set they are below $1/2$, and the remaining such coefficients have finite maximum below one. Hence the kernel is exactly $A_{<1}$. Finite coefficient convolution proves multiplicativity of this reduction map, and lifting the finitely many coefficients of any polynomial proves surjectivity. It therefore induces the asserted isomorphism, preserving constants and variables.

source.place: BGR Theorem 6.3.5/1, finite map implies finite reduction map. Independently read in Temkin, A new proof of the Gerritzen-Grauert theorem, introduction printed p.2 and section 2 (definition of reduction); https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Gerritzen_Grauert.pdf. BGR archival copy WANTED; source is not locally present.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-affinoid-canonical-reduction] to $\varphi:A\to C$. Both algebras are nonzero, reduced, and strict affinoids over the given complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field; finiteness was supplied in step 1. The lemma gives a map $\widetilde\varphi:\widetilde A\to\widetilde C$ and finitely many module generators $\bar e_1,\ldots,\bar e_N$ for $\widetilde C$ over $\widetilde A$. Choose representatives $e_j\in C_{\le1}$. The lemma also gives $\rho(\varphi(U_i))\le1$, so those variable images have representatives in the required unit ball.

source.place: BGR Theorem 6.3.5/1, finite map implies finite reduction map. Independently read in Temkin, A new proof of the Gerritzen-Grauert theorem, introduction printed p.2 and section 2 (definition of reduction); https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Gerritzen_Grauert.pdf. BGR archival copy WANTED; source is not locally present.

proof.text: For any $\bar c\in\widetilde C$, module generation gives $\bar c=\sum_{j=1}^N\widetilde\varphi(P_j)\bar e_j$ with $P_j\in\kappa[U_1,\ldots,U_d]$, using step 2. Each summand is a polynomial over $\kappa$ in the classes of $\varphi(U_1),\ldots,\varphi(U_d),e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus these $d+N$ representatives in $C_{\le1}$ give the requested algebra generators. No assumption that the reduction map is surjective, and no finite generation of the full power-bounded ring over the valuation ring, is needed.
